question: Should OpenClaw adopt a first-class agent-ID rename contract, including the policy for explicit workspace paths and the required participation model for plugin-owned state?
rationale: The requested behavior introduces a new destructive migration workflow whose path ownership and plugin compatibility semantics cannot be selected safely from source-level mechanics alone.

options.title: Sponsor a transactional rename design
options.body: Define the public CLI/gateway contract, preserve explicit workspace paths by default, move only owned defaults, and require verified plugin migration participation.

options.title: Limit the scope to core state first
options.body: Ship a narrowly defined core-only rename after documenting that plugins with state prevent or defer the operation until a compatible contract exists.

options.title: Keep rename unsupported
options.body: Retain the current safety boundary and document that established agent IDs are immutable after state creation.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a transactional rename design
recommendation.body: Define the public CLI/gateway contract, preserve explicit workspace paths by default, move only owned defaults, and require verified plugin migration participation.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter has supplied the concrete problem framing, while current-main feature-history owners could not be established because read-only repository commands were unavailable.
